premises.text: Cookie is a Keurig-like robotic cooker for fresh pre-portioned meal trays controlled from a phone
premises.evidence_span: Think of it as a Keurig for cooking fresh food using robotics. In the same way that Keurig simplified the process of making coffee down to insert a cup and press a button, Cookie delivers that same experience in making home-cooked meals with multiple trays of fresh ingredients

premises.text: Busy students (and later professionals/moms) need convenient ways to eat right without cooking skill
premises.evidence_span: how can my fellow classmates and I manage our new responsibilities while still continuing to eat right?

premises.text: Foodie plus Cookie enable recipe selection, store purchases, scheduling, and chef-taught cooking motions
premises.evidence_span: They can specify the recipes step by step. They can even teach Cookie to move like they do by tracing out a motion on their phone

premises.text: Unit economics: meals ~$4, device $600 or subscription rental, competing with frozen but using fresh food
premises.evidence_span: A Serenity meal is typically priced at around $4 per meal. The app is free, and cookie will retail at $600

premises.text: Pre-portioned kits address food waste and overconsumption/obesity by reducing prep work and excess ingredients
premises.evidence_span: An average American household lets 40% of the fresh ingredients that they buy spoil. 69% of Americans are considered obese

domains.name: Meal kit economics and waste reduction

value.text: Make food better by delivering push-button fresh cooked meals

causal_links.evidence_span: help conserve food and encourage healthier eating habits

notes: Hardware detail of arm/cooktop folded into Cookie system premise. Closing mission slogan used as value with product benefit warrant elsewhere.
